clue.text: Old maid puts doctor under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the word for doctor below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to doctor is to rig, as in tampering with results or accounts

explanation.surface: A spinster is leaning hard on her physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, to tamper with or rig; 'under' sets it below P in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: a prim, fussy, strait-laced person of either sex who is easily shocked.

clue.text: Boxer Billy who sings in French — yes, soprano

parts.note: Billy Joel is the American singer-songwriter, and his surname is used
the French word for yes is oui
S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A fighter called Billy takes the high part in a French song.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American heavyweight champion of the world from 1937 to 1949, nicknamed the Brown Bomber.

clue.text: Servant girl with bible standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England
AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible of 1611

explanation.surface: A maid rises to her feet holding a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns the whole run LASS + AV upside down in this down entry. AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal subordinate who owed service to a lord, so loosely any dependant or underling.

clue.text: Work in trouble

definitions.meaning: to massage a cream or oil into a surface with pressure
a snag or difficulty, as in Hamlet's line about what dreams may come

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to massage something into a surface, and a snag or difficulty as in Hamlet's soliloquy.

clue.text: Covered in grass, circuits got worse

indicators.note: the circuits are covered in grass, so their word sits inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
laps are circuits of a racetrack

explanation.surface: An overgrown racetrack deteriorated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a patient who slipped back into illness after improving deteriorated again.

clue.text: A river runs through bend in northern town

indicators.note: the three letters pass through the middle of the word for bend

parts.note: to bow is to bend, as a branch bows under weight
R is the map abbreviation for river
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A watercourse flows round a curve in a place up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like the surface's verb but is the cricket abbreviation R; 'through' puts A, R, R inside BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shipbuilding port in Cumbria, north-west England, whose full name adds -in-Furness.

clue.text: When playing, actor niven also relaxed

indicators.note: playing suggests letters in motion, so the three words that follow are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: On stage the film star David Niven seemed at ease too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When playing' is the anagram signal for ACTOR NIVEN ALSO; the surface suggests the film star David Niven at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for a style: chatty, informal speech or writing is easy-going rather than stiff.

clue.text: After bible classes, will copy sinner

indicators.note: the copy of the will comes after the classes, fixing the order of the two pieces

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
probate is the officially certified copy of a will

explanation.surface: Once scripture lessons are over, someone promises to imitate a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' reads as a future tense but is the legal document: probate is the certified copy of a will. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unprincipled, morally depraved person, originally one rejected by God.

clue.text: Flags down vehicle for this designer?

definitions.text: Flags down vehicle for this designer?

parts.words: Flags down vehicle for this designer?
parts.note: flags are paving stones, down on the ground, and a vehicle is a medium for expression: someone who chalks pictures on the street uses them as a canvas

explanation.surface: Someone waves at a car to stop it for a stylist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: one who chalks pictures on paving slabs uses the flagstones underfoot as a medium.

clue.text: Border crossing over here and there

indicators.note: the word for border goes across, straddling the letter for over

parts.note: to abut is to border on, to share a boundary with
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Frontier checkpoints are scattered in various places.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adverb: things strewn around lie in various scattered places.

clue.text: Persuades train station to keep gutted livestock

indicators.note: the reworked station keeps, holds inside it, what is left of the livestock
to train is to drill or school into shape, so the next word's letters are put in a new order
gutting removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone convinces a railway stop to hold slaughtered farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is not a railway noun but the anagram signal, turning its neighbour into TASINTO; 'gutted' empties the animals and 'to keep' tucks what remains inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: convinces someone by argument to do something.

clue.text: Is this produced with end of trial?

definitions.text: Is this produced with end of trial?

indicators.note: with joins the following letter onto the word for produced

parts.note: gave means produced or yielded, as a cow gave milk

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an item was brought out when a court case finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, a judge's hammer banged as a case closes, while 'produced with end of trial' also builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hammer a judge or auctioneer bangs to bring proceedings to a close.

clue.text: Cruising behind wind

parts.note: seat and behind are both words for the buttocks
to ravel is to wind or tangle thread; this wind rhymes with kind

explanation.surface: A yacht sails along with the breeze at its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' is a noun, the buttocks, and 'wind' is the verb that rhymes with kind, not a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cruise is one form of voyaging by ship.

clue.text: Passing comment while couple occupying farm sold us ground

indicators.note: the two inner pieces occupy, sit inside, the reworked letters
ground as in milled or crushed, so the three words before it are broken up and reordered

parts.note: as means while: she sang as she worked
a couple is two of something

explanation.surface: A remark made in passing as a pair living on a farm sell us some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is not land but the anagram signal, giving FAMOUSLRDS, which 'occupying' then splits open. 'Passing' in the definition means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A dying person's final utterance, or ironically a rash remark soon proved wrong.

clue.text: Devour jars of peanuts

indicators.note: to jar is to jolt or shake, so the two words after it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone greedily eats whole containers of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' is a verb here, jolts, rather than glass containers: it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to eat something greedily and with relish.

clue.text: Likely to forget a host? Oddly, needs him on board

indicators.note: the host has the picked letters on board, carried inside like passengers on a ship

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: An absent-minded party-giver strangely requires a man to be aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' applies to both following words run together, letters 1, 3, 5 and 7; 'on board' tucks them inside a master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for someone suffering memory loss, who cannot recall things.

clue.text: Fell over during shortened rest

indicators.note: during places the first two pieces within the span of the word for shortened

parts.note: cut means shortened, as in a cut version of a film
a fell is a hill or stretch of upland in northern England
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled during a nap that was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a past tense but is the noun, a northern English upland; 'during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym as a verb: to relax and take it easy.

clue.text: Ruckus about one's lawyer showing contempt

indicators.note: the word for ruckus goes about, around, the other two pieces

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or commotion
one is the Roman numeral I, and the possessive adds its S
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over somebody's solicitor being scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: scorn for something thought unworthy.

clue.text: Work ending, so claimed benefit

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or manipulate it, so the letters of the next two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: The job is finishing, so someone applied for welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' at the front tells you to rearrange ENDING SO. In Britain, to sign on is to register as unemployed and receive state payments.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom: registered as unemployed at the job centre to receive state payments.

clue.text: Having fit iron glove, it can't go unnoticed

indicators.note: a fit is a convulsion, so the words that follow are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the four letters

explanation.surface: An iron gauntlet that fits well is too conspicuous to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having fit' is the anagram signal, a fit being a convulsion: IRON GLOVE IT CANT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to journey under a disguised or concealed identity so nobody recognises you.

clue.text: Sandwich is one yours truly's thrown up — it's got a little horse in it

indicators.note: the upturned word has got the horse within it, as the closing words in it confirm
in a down clue, thrown up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: yours truly is how a writer refers to me
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: Someone vomits a sandwich that turns out to contain a tiny horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Sandwich gave his name to the snack, hence 'Sandwich is one'. 'thrown up' gives EM, and 'it's got ... in it' wraps that round the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Earl of Sandwich is a person after whom something is named.

clue.text: Red cabbage wants nothing in spring

indicators.note: wanting nothing in means lacking any contents, so the word loses its inner letters

parts.note: cole is an old word for cabbage, as in coleslaw
to spring is to rise, as in springing up from a chair

explanation.surface: A purple vegetable needs no attention during the early growing season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants nothing in' empties an old word for cabbage of its inner letters. 'Red cabbage' reads as one vegetable but splits between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of a shade: a bright, deep pinkish colour named after the French for cherry.

clue.text: This be poor lit badly written

definitions.text: This be poor lit badly written

indicators.note: writing the letters badly means setting the three words before it down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A rustic critic declares a book to be weak literature, clumsily composed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, with 'This' pointing at it; 'badly written' rearranges BE POOR LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A book churned out quickly just to earn money, with little literary merit.

clue.text: Wise seabird circling island

indicators.note: the bird circles, goes round, the letter for island

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A clever gull flies round a small isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is not an adjective but a surname: the shorter half of the British comedy duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by surname: the first name of the comedian who partnered Eric Morecambe on British television.

clue.text: More wheels? Pretty much — works fantastic!

definitions.note: a collection of mythological poems or tales, several works of fantasy under one title

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn right round, so the word is read backwards
pretty much means nearly all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: added means more or extra, as in added sugar

explanation.surface: Someone asks if extra tyres are fitted and is thrilled with the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty much' drops the last letter of ADDED and 'wheels' turns ADDE round. The Eddas are Old Norse collections of myth, hence 'works fantastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval Icelandic collection of Norse myths and heroic poems, literature full of fantasy.

clue.text: Really describing a good man as offensive

indicators.note: to describe is to trace a line round, as a compass describes a circle, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: nay is an old emphatic word meaning indeed or in point of fact
a saint, abbreviated St, is a good man

explanation.surface: Someone is honestly calling a decent chap objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is the container signal, in its geometric sense of tracing a line round something; the good man is a saint, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unpleasant or disgusting, causing revulsion.

clue.text: Virgin — no slag?

definitions.meaning: pristine and untouched, as in virgin forest
slag is mining waste, also called spoil, so land with none on it is whimsically free of spoil

explanation.surface: Someone insists a woman is chaste, not at all promiscuous.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a slag is a promiscuous woman, which the surface plays on; the second definition wants the mining sense, where slag is spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean pristine: untouched land, and whimsically a site with no mining waste, called spoil, on it.

clue.text: Old woman beginning to tie knot

parts.note: old woman is slang for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An elderly lady starts fastening a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thick tangled mass, as of hair, or as a verb to tangle.
